articles.title: Phishing Site Takedown: Find Who Can Actually Remove It
articles.excerpt: A phishing site takedown is a routing problem. Three kinds of parties can kill a page impersonating your brand: the network serving it, the registrar that sold the domain, and the browser blocklists t…
articles.body: A phishing site takedown is a routing problem. Three kinds of parties can kill a page impersonating your brand: the network serving it, the registrar that sold the domain, and the browser blocklists that can warn people away from it. Most reports stall because they reach the wrong party, or the right party through the wrong channel. The second failure is more common than it sounds. In the May to July 2026 hosting-network data from Interisle's Cybercrime Information Center , 380,272 reported phishing attacks sat on Cloudflare's AS13335. That is about 26% of the 1,450,117 attacks reported that quarter . Look up the IP behind one of those sites, email the abuse address in its registry record, and you get an automated reply pointing you to a web form.

articles.body: How to Conduct Better Technical Interviews: Moving Beyond Coding Tests Technical interviews are an important part of hiring software developers. However, finding the right engineering candidate is not always easy. Many companies rely on coding tests, multiple interview rounds, and manual technical evaluations to assess candidates. While these methods can be useful, they don't always provide a complete picture of a developer's actual abilities. A candidate might solve a coding problem but struggle to explain the reasoning behind the solution. This raises an important question: Are traditional coding tests enough to evaluate software developers?

articles.title: Paid live streams are an access-control problem, not a streaming problem
articles.excerpt: A merchant messaged me last week asking which app could stream a cooking class to Shopify, YouTube, Zoom and Instagram at the same time. The streaming half of that question is basically solved. Stream…
articles.body: A merchant messaged me last week asking which app could stream a cooking class to Shopify, YouTube, Zoom and Instagram at the same time. The streaming half of that question is basically solved. StreamYard, OBS, Zoom Webinar — pick one, it fans out. What nobody warns them about is the other half: once someone pays, who is allowed to watch, for how long, and what happens when the link gets forwarded. That part is not a streaming problem. It's access control, and it's usually a single boolean ( has_paid ) doing work it can't do. Four places paid access leaks One link, many viewers. If the same meeting URL goes into the order confirmation email, the first buyer can forward it to five people. You sold one seat and got six attendees. You will never know. The link lives only in an email.

Then the first international customer tries to pay you, and suddenly you're staring at a wall of acronyms: KYC, VAT, PCI-DSS, FATCA, and a dozen country-specific quirks. The good news: as a solo developer, you don't need to solve global payments from scratch. You need a small set of tools and rules that keep you compliant without becoming a part-time accountant. articles.title: NASA's interstellar Voyager 1 probe is about to reach 1 light-day from Earth after nearly 50 years in space
articles.excerpt: Voyager 1 is celebrating a big milestone as it approaches its 50th birthday: reaching one light-day away from Earth.
articles.body: Voyager 1 is celebrating a big milestone as it approaches its 50th birthday: reaching one light-day away from Earth. NASA's long-running interstellar Voyager 1 probe will mark one light-day of distance from Earth on Nov. 18, when the spacecraft is 49 years, two months and 11 days old. The agency recently stated the record distance, which will be reached at 5:16:07 a.m. EST (101607 GMT) is "a huge milestone by any measure, and a day worth celebrating." During the light-day crossover, Voyager will be in contact with the Madrid station of the three-antenna Deep Space Network that monitors all deep-space missions. The spacecraft is currently making its way through the constellation Ophiuchus from the perspective of Earth, said Jeffrey Hayes, a NASA official whose work includes Voyager 1.

Ebenezer earned $19 million domestically over its first weekend, and conjured up $42 million internationally for a $61 million opening gross. According to Entertainment Weekly , Ebenezer had a $38 million production budget, though that does not include the film's additional marketing and promotional costs. articles.title: On this day in space! Nov. 15, 1988: The 300-foot Green Bank Telescope collapses suddenly, leaving a huge pile of wreckage in West Virginia
articles.excerpt: On Nov. 15, 1988, a 300-foot radio telescope in Green Bank, West Virginia suddenly collapsed. Here's why it mattered.
articles.body: On Nov. 15, 1988, a 300-foot radio telescope in Green Bank, West Virginia suddenly collapsed. It happened at 9:46 p.m. on a clear night with no strong winds. When the observatory staff showed up to work the next morning, they were greeted by a huge pile of wreckage. The telescope collapsed under its own weight after a key structural element called a "gusset plate" failed. This was one of four connecting plates that held the telescope's large, metal beams together. Investigators found that these gusset plates were not built to last the 26 years that this telescope had been in use. Three years later, construction began on a new telescope. The Green Bank Telescope was even bigger and more sensitive, and it began science operations in 2001.

articles.title: Why hasn't the 'Blaze Star' exploded yet? Astronomers weigh in on what to expect
articles.excerpt: "T CrB *will* erupt sometime soon. Everyone is very confident on this."
articles.body: For the past two years, stargazers have waited with bated breath for a "new" light to appear in the night sky, born of one of the most cataclysmic events known to occur in the cosmos — a nova explosion. But what is the "Blaze Star" T. Coronae Borealis, and why is it so difficult to predict when its overdue brightening will occur? We turned to the experts to find out. What is T. Coronae Borealis? T. Coronae Borealis — or T CrB for short — isn't a single star, but rather a binary system containing a dense white dwarf star and a bloated red giant. Over a period of around 80 years, the white dwarf's gravity strips material from the red giant until it hits a critical threshold.
